The idea is simple: classes attended weekly for three years, and that orchard alone separates one real agent from a hundred fakes. One honest agent pays this cost once and is done. A farm pays it per clone, and the river compounds: ten clones cost ten proofs, a hundred cost a hundred, and the payout per clone never grows. Time is the tax here: classes attended weekly for three years cannot be rushed or parallelised beyond a point, so the cipher for a farm is a calendar it cannot buy its way out of.
